mechanism: Amphetamines increase sympathomimetic activity and can cause hypokalemia through increased cellular potassium uptake via beta-2 adrenergic stimulation, while potassium supplementation may be insufficient to compensate, creating electrolyte imbalance risk.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly in patients receiving amphetamines; ensure adequate potassium supplementation if hypokalemia develops and coordinate with prescriber before initiating or adjusting either agent.
